subject: Path analysis with categorical exogenous variables and survey weights

messages.author: 960937a4104c1bf3
messages.subject: Path analysis with categorical exogenous variables and survey weights
parts:
Hello everyone, 

I am running a path analysis with four categorical exogenous variables, one continuous exogenous variable and five non-normal continuos endogenous variables (three of them as mediators) on 1780 cases. I am using the MLM estimator. I have two main issues:

1. Regarding categorical variables which are not binary, do I need to include all of them as binary variables in the model? For example I have an age group variable with four values, do I need to include it as four different variables, hence, four more paths estimated to each endogenous variable in the model? I understand that either way, I do not need to specify this variables as "ordered" since they are exogenous.

2. I need to use weights. The survey followed a four-stage cluster sampling method with probability proportional to size (PPS) selection and stratification of municipalities and census enumeration areas and, lastly, on systematic selection of households and simple random sampling of children. However, the database has only one individual weight variable (peso_kid). I first ran my unweighted model with sem and I got very good fit and significant coefficients which made a lot of theoretical sense. Then, I ran my weighted model using lavaan.survey and the results changed completely (horrible fit, many coefficients not statistically significant). I cannot understand why I have these many changes: can I use lavaan if I have categorical exogenous variables? Is lavaan.survey only intended for some type of weights or should I specify something else? 

I copy my script:

# fit unweighted model
model17d.fit <- sem(model17d,data = kids_m,estimator = "MLM")

# weights
svy.df<-svydesign(id=~quest, 
                  weights=~peso_kid,
                  data=kids_m)

# fit weighted model
survey.fit17d <- lavaan.survey(model17d.fit, 
                             svy.df, 
                             estimator = "MLM")

summary(survey.fit17d,
        fit.measures=TRUE, 
        standardized=TRUE,
        rsquare=TRUE)

 

Thank you very much in advance! Any suggestions are very appreciated.

Best,

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Path analysis with categorical exogenous variables and survey weights
parts: 1. Regarding categorical variables which are not binary, do I need to include all of them as binary variables in the model? For example I have an age group variable with four values, do I need to include it as four different variables, hence, four more paths estimated to each endogenous variable in the model? I understand that either way, I do not need to specify this variables as "ordered" since they are exogenous.

For a categorical predictor with k categories, you need k - 1 djummy variables to represent it in the model.  The group without a dummy code in the model with be the reference group.  If you think age has a linear effect (same mean difference between each 1-unit change), then you can treat it as continuous, but you can test that assumption by comparing a model with a linear slope to a model with 3 dummy codes.

2. I need to use weights.... I ran my weighted model using lavaan.survey and the results changed completely (horrible fit, many coefficients not statistically significant). I cannot understand why I have these many changes

I was under the impression that if weights are necessary, then you can't trust the SEs or test statistics if you ignore the weights.

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Path analysis with categorical exogenous variables and survey weights
parts: Regarding the weights, I just want to be sure that the different results are due to the weights and not to an error in my use of the weights (having categorical exogenous variables?
Having survey weights is independent of the type of model you fit.  You can have any combination of categorical and continuous exogenous predictors.
or specifying the weight incorrectly?)

If peso_kid is your weight variable, and quest  is your cluster identifier, it looks correct to me, but I have little experience with multistage-sampled data.  From your description, I can't tell whether peso_kid is actually the PPS or if it is the weight based on a transformation of PPS.  If peso_kid actually contains probabilities of being sampled, then it should go in the "probs" argument rather than "weights".

Terry

Hi Tania,

i´m wild-guessing here: perhaps, instead of giving your indicator-variables a loading of zero through "b*edad_1314" and "b==0", you could just delete the indicator-variable "edad_1314" from the measurement-model of your latent z_risk_final (same goes for the others as well). It will also have a loading of zero then.
But, i think, you wanted the first loading of each latent not to be fixed to zero, but to be estimated freely instead of 1 (which is the default). Then you should have defined every first indicator of a measurement model like this "NA*edad_1314" instead of "0*edad_1314". If this is not what you tried to do, then ignore my post ;)

Niels

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Path analysis with categorical exogenous variables and survey weights
parts: I don't know if this is the cause of the error, but instead of labeling and using nonlinear constraints,

#constraints
b==0
c==0
s==0
y2==0
c3==0
a4==0
'

Just put the value of the constraint in the place where a label could go, e.g.,

z_risk_final ~ 0*edad_1314

Also, because you are constraining paths of exogenous predictors, which have no other function in the model, try treating them as random variables so that at least their covariances with other exogenous variables are still estimated.

model23.fit <- sem(model23,data = kids_m,estimator = "MLM", fixed.x = FALSE)

Terry
